ad.name: Andorra
ad.symbolism: The coat of arms combines the symbols of the Bishop of Urgell, the Count of Foix, Catalonia and Béarn, the historic powers tied to Andorra, under the motto 'Virtue United is Stronger'. The blue, yellow and red link the country to the lands historically connected with it.

ae.name: United Arab Emirates
ae.symbolism: The red, green, white and black are the Pan-Arab colours, symbolising Arab unity. Red stands for the energy and sacrifices of the people, green for growth and prosperity, white for peace and purity, and black for dignity.

af.name: Afghanistan
af.symbolism: The white field stands for the purity of faith and government. The black inscription is the shahada, the Islamic declaration of faith.

ag.name: Antigua and Barbuda
ag.symbolism: The V shape stands for victory, and the red sides for the energy of the people. The black stands for African ancestry and the rising sun for the dawn of a new era, while blue means hope and white recalls the sand; together the colours also evoke soil, sun, sea and sand.

ai.name: Anguilla
ai.symbolism: The Blue Ensign and Union Jack mark Anguilla's British ties. The three dolphins in a circle stand for unity, strength and endurance, the white background for peace, and the light blue for the sea, faith, youth and hope.

al.name: Albania
al.symbolism: The red field stands for bravery, strength, valour and bloodshed. The black double-headed eagle is the traditional symbol of the Albanians, and the emblem of the hero Skanderbeg who led the revolt against the Ottomans.

am.name: Armenia
am.symbolism: Red stands for the Armenian highlands, the people's struggle for survival and the Christian faith. Blue is for the peaceful Armenian skies, and orange for the nation's talent and hard work.

ao.name: Angola
ao.symbolism: The red stripe represents the blood shed in the fight against colonialism, and the black stripe stands for Africa. The yellow half cog and machete symbolise workers and farmers, and the star stands for progress and international solidarity.

aq.name: Antarctica
aq.flagNote: Antarctica has no official flag: no country owns it and no institution can adopt one, so every flag in use is unofficial.

ar.name: Argentina
ar.symbolism: The light blue and white stripes are popularly linked to the sky and clouds. The golden Sun of May at the centre has a human face and 32 rays, and one historian has read it as a representation of the Inca sun god Inti.

as.name: American Samoa
as.symbolism: The bald eagle clutches a war club, for the government's power, and a fly whisk, for the wisdom of traditional Samoan leaders. The red, white and blue stand for the colours traditionally used by both the United States and Samoa, and with the eagle for the territory's ties to the United States.

at.name: Austria
at.symbolism: Legend says Duke Leopold V's white tunic was soaked in blood in battle, leaving only a white band where his belt had been, which gave the red-white-red stripes. The colours come from the coat of arms of the Babenberg dynasty.

au.name: Australia
au.symbolism: The Union Jack in the corner recalls Australia's British origins. The large seven-pointed Commonwealth Star stands for the six states and the territories, and the five stars of the Southern Cross represent the constellation seen in the southern sky.

aw.name: Aruba
aw.symbolism: The light blue stands for the sea, and the two yellow stripes for abundance, such as gold and aloe farming and tourism. The red four-pointed star represents the four compass points that Aruba's people came from, and its white border stands for peace.

ax.name: Åland Islands
ax.symbolism: The red cross within the yellow-edged Nordic cross symbolises Finland, which the Åland Islands belong to.

az.name: Azerbaijan
az.symbolism: Blue stands for Azerbaijan's Turkic identity, red for progress and a modern state, and green for Islam. The crescent is a marker of Islam, and the eight points of the star are thought to stand for the eight Turkic peoples.

ba.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
ba.symbolism: The three points of the yellow triangle stand for the three constituent peoples, the Bosniaks, Croats and Serbs, and the triangle also approximates the shape of the country. The white stars on blue evoke Europe and are meant to be infinite in number.

bb.name: Barbados
bb.symbolism: The ultramarine bands stand for the sea and sky and the gold band for the sand. The black trident head, broken from the old colonial badge, symbolises breaking away from the colonial past, and its three points stand for the principles of democracy.

bd.name: Bangladesh
bd.symbolism: The green stands for the lushness of the country's landscape. The red disc represents the blood shed in the Liberation War and is also read as the rising sun.

be.name: Belgium
be.symbolism: The black, yellow and red were taken from the coat of arms of the Duchy of Brabant, and correspond to the lions of the historic Belgian lands: red for Hainaut, Limburg and Luxembourg, yellow for Brabant, and black for Flanders and Namur.

bf.name: Burkina Faso
bf.symbolism: Red represents the revolution and green the country's agriculture and wealth. The yellow star is the guiding light of the revolution.

bg.name: Bulgaria
bg.symbolism: The flag is a national symbol that, by law, expresses the independence and sovereignty of the Bulgarian state.

bh.name: Bahrain
bh.symbolism: The red stands for the blood of martyrs and Bahrain's battles, and the white for peace. The five points of the serrated edge symbolise the five pillars of Islam.

bi.name: Burundi
bi.symbolism: The white saltire stands for peace, the green for hope in the nation's future and the red for the suffering during the struggle for freedom. The three stars on the white disc stand for the Hutu, Twa and Tutsi peoples and for the national motto of unity, work and progress.

bj.name: Benin
bj.symbolism: Green stands for the hope of a new democracy, yellow for the treasures of the nation, and red for the courage of the ancestors. They are the Pan-African colours.

bl.name: Saint Barthélemy
bl.flagNote: Uses the French national flag; the arms-on-white flag used locally is unofficial.

bm.name: Bermuda
bm.symbolism: The Red Ensign and Union Jack mark Bermuda's British ties. The arms show a lion holding a shield with the wreck of the Sea Venture, the ship whose wreck led to the island's settlement.

bn.name: Brunei
bn.symbolism: Yellow is traditionally the colour of royalty in Southeast Asia and here stands for the Sultan, while the white and black diagonal stripes represent the chief ministers, the wazirs. The red emblem shows a crescent for Islam, a parasol for the monarchy, and raised hands for the benevolence of the government.

bo.name: Bolivia
bo.symbolism: Red represents the blood shed by the nation's heroes for the birth and preservation of the Republic, yellow the country's wealth and resources, and green the richness of its natural areas and hope.

bq.name: Caribbean Netherlands
bq.flagNote: The three islands together have no flag; Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba each have their own, and the Dutch national flag is used for the whole.

br.name: Brazil
br.symbolism: Green once stood for the House of Braganza of the first emperor and yellow for the House of Habsburg of his wife. The blue globe reflects the sky over Rio de Janeiro on the day the republic was proclaimed, with one star for each state and the Federal District, and the motto 'Ordem e Progresso' (order and progress), taken from positivist philosophy.

bs.name: Bahamas
bs.symbolism: Aquamarine represents the surrounding sea and gold the sun and the land's natural resources. The black triangle stands for the strength, vigour and force of the Bahamian people.

bt.name: Bhutan
bt.symbolism: The white Druk, the thunder dragon of Bhutanese myth, gives the country its name, 'Land of the Thunder Dragon'. Its white colour signifies the purity of inner thoughts and deeds, and it holds a jewel in each claw. Yellow signifies the civil authority of the king and orange the Buddhist spiritual tradition.

bv.name: Bouvet Island
bv.symbolism: Bouvet Island is an uninhabited Norwegian territory and uses the flag of Norway. The Nordic cross represents Christianity, and red, white and blue were chosen as colours of freedom.

bw.name: Botswana
bw.symbolism: The light blue represents water and rainfall, which is crucial to the agriculture of the arid country. The black stripe with a white frame stands for racial harmony.

by.name: Belarus
by.symbolism: The red-and-white decorative pattern at the hoist is a traditional Belarusian one, of the kind used in woven rushnyk cloths. There is no official interpretation of the colours, but the president has said red represents freedom and the sacrifice of the nation's forefathers, and green life.

bz.name: Belize
bz.symbolism: The blue and red come from the colours of the country's two main political parties. The coat of arms recalls the logging industry with woodcutters, tools and mahogany trees, and its wreath of 50 leaves marks the year the party that led to independence came to power.

ca.name: Canada
ca.symbolism: Red and white are Canada's official colours. The single red maple leaf is a Canadian emblem, and its 11 points were chosen after wind tunnel tests rather than for any symbolic meaning.

cc.name: Cocos (Keeling) Islands
cc.symbolism: Green and gold are Australia's national colours. The palm tree on the gold disc represents the islands' tropical flora, the crescent the Cocos Malays and Islam, and the Southern Cross is a symbol of Australia and the Southern Hemisphere.

cd.name: DR Congo
cd.symbolism: The sky blue stands for peace, the red stripe for the blood of the country's martyrs, and the yellow edging for wealth. The yellow star symbolises a bright future.

cf.name: Central African Republic
cf.symbolism: Blue and white stand for France and green and yellow for Africa, joined by the vertical red stripe, which symbolises blood and the respect Europeans and Africans should have for each other. The yellow star of independence stands for the country's aspirations for a vibrant future.

cg.name: Republic of the Congo
cg.symbolism: The diagonal bands use the Pan-African colours. Green stands for the agriculture and forests of the Republic of the Congo and yellow for the friendship and nobility of its people; the meaning of the red is officially left unexplained.

ch.name: Switzerland
ch.symbolism: The white cross is described by the Swiss Federal Council as both the Christian cross and the field sign of the Old Confederacy.

ci.name: Côte d'Ivoire
ci.symbolism: Orange recalls the country's rich and generous land and the struggle of a young people for emancipation, white stands for peace and purity, and green for hope for a better future.

ck.name: Cook Islands
ck.symbolism: The Union Jack in the canton recalls the islands' British ties. The ring of 15 white stars represents the 15 islands, and the blue stands for the ocean and the peaceful nature of the inhabitants.

cl.name: Chile
cl.symbolism: White stands for the snow-covered Andes, red for the blood shed for independence, and blue for the sky and the Pacific Ocean. The white star, linked to the Mapuche symbol of Venus, is a guide to progress and honour.

cm.name: Cameroon
cm.symbolism: The colours are Pan-African. Green represents the forests of the south, red unity, and yellow the sun and savannas of the north. The yellow star on the red band is the star of unity.

cn.name: China
cn.symbolism: The red field symbolises the Communist Revolution. The large star represents the Chinese Communist Party and the four smaller stars the unity of the people under it, originally the working class, the peasantry, the urban petty bourgeoisie and the national bourgeoisie.

co.name: Colombia
co.symbolism: Yellow stands for sovereignty and justice, blue for loyalty and vigilance, and red for the victory of the battles for independence.

cr.name: Costa Rica
cr.symbolism: Blue stands for the sky, opportunity and perseverance, white for clear thinking and wisdom, and the wider red stripe for the warmth of the Costa Rican people and the first rays of true independence.

cu.name: Cuba
cu.symbolism: The three blue stripes represent the three departments the island was then divided into, and the white stripes the purity of the patriot cause. The red triangle symbolises strength and constancy, with Masonic associations of equality.

cv.name: Cabo Verde
cv.symbolism: The blue stands for the ocean and sky, and the ten yellow stars represent the ten islands. The white and red stripes stand for the road to nation-building through peace and effort.

cw.name: Curaçao
cw.symbolism: Blue represents the sea and sky, with the yellow stripe between them for the bright sun. The two white stars stand for Curaçao and Klein Curaçao, and their five points for the five continents the people descend from.

cx.name: Christmas Island
cx.symbolism: Green stands for the island's land and blue for the sea. The golden bosun bird, native to the island, is a symbol of the island.

cy.name: Cyprus
cy.symbolism: The copper-coloured silhouette of the island stands for its large copper deposits, long linked with its name. The two green olive branches symbolise peace between the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities, and the white field is another symbol of peace.

cz.name: Czechia
cz.symbolism: White is the traditional colour of Bohemia and red stands for Moravia and the bloodshed for the state's freedom. The blue triangle stands for impartiality and sovereignty.

de.name: Germany
de.symbolism: Black, red and gold are associated with unity, freedom and democracy, and come from the liberal and nationalist movements. They are said to derive from the uniforms of a volunteer corps that fought against Napoleon.

dj.name: Djibouti
dj.symbolism: Light blue stands for the sky and sea and for the Somalis, green for the earth and for the Afars, and white for peace. The red star represents unity, the blood shed by the martyrs of independence, and Djibouti as one of the five regions inhabited by Somali people.

dk.name: Denmark
dk.symbolism: Known as the Dannebrog, it shows a white Nordic cross, which represents Christianity. Legend says the flag fell from the sky during a battle and brought the Danes victory.

dm.name: Dominica
dm.symbolism: Green stands for the island's lush vegetation, and the cross for the Trinity and Christianity, with its yellow, black and white bands standing for the native people, the fertile soil and the pure water. The red disc stands for justice and holds the Sisserou parrot, ringed by ten green stars for the parishes.

do.name: Dominican Republic
do.symbolism: Blue stands for liberty, red for the blood of heroes, and the white cross for salvation and the peace and unity of the people. The coat of arms shows an open Bible above a cross, with the motto 'God, Fatherland, Liberty', reflecting the Christian ideals of the flag's designer.

dz.name: Algeria
dz.symbolism: Green is the colour of Islam, and red and white are both linked to jihad. The crescent is a symbol of Islam, and the five-pointed star is read as the five pillars of Islam or the five daily prayers.

ec.name: Ecuador
ec.symbolism: The wide yellow stripe stands for crops and fertile soil, blue for the ocean and clear skies, and red for the blood spilled by the heroes who died for freedom. The coat of arms stands for the country's geography: Mount Chimborazo, the Guayas River and a steamship whose caduceus represents trade, with the outstretched condor above for power, greatness and strength.

ee.name: Estonia
ee.symbolism: A popular reading by the poet Martin Lipp has blue standing for the sky above Estonians, black for the soil of the homeland, and white for purity, hard work and commitment.

eg.name: Egypt
eg.symbolism: The red, white and black are Pan-Arab colours: red for the Egyptians' blood shed in the war against colonisation, white for the purity of their hearts, and black for the darkness that was overcome. The central Eagle of Saladin is the national emblem and echoes the Egyptian vulture, a bird sacred in ancient Egyptian religion.

eh.name: Western Sahara
eh.symbolism: The Pan-Arab colours stand for hope of returning to their lands (green), peace and purity (white), grief for the martyrs (black) and the blood they spilled (red). The star represents an Arab republic and the crescent a Muslim country. It is the flag of the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic, which claims the territory.

er.name: Eritrea
er.symbolism: Green stands for the country's agriculture and livestock, blue for the bounty of the sea, and the red triangle for the bloodshed in the struggle for independence. The gold olive wreath has 30 leaves for the thirty years of that struggle.

es.name: Spain
es.symbolism: The red and yellow stripes come from the historic Aragonese crown. The coat of arms on the wide yellow band contains the pillars of Hercules and the symbols of the old kingdoms, including Castile, León, Aragon and Navarre.

et.name: Ethiopia
et.symbolism: Red stands for the blood spilled in defence of Ethiopia, yellow for peace and harmony between its ethnic and religious groups, and green for hope or the fertile land. The star on the blue disc stands for a bright future, and its rays for the equality of all Ethiopians.

fi.name: Finland
fi.symbolism: The white represents the snow that covers the land in winter, and the blue cross the country's thousands of lakes and the sky.

fj.name: Fiji
fj.symbolism: The light blue stands for the Pacific Ocean, which is central to the islanders' lives, and the Union Jack for the links with the United Kingdom. The shield stands for agriculture and those British ties: a British lion holds a cocoa pod above sugar cane, a coconut palm, bananas and a dove of peace.

fk.name: Falkland Islands
fk.symbolism: The Blue Ensign and Union Jack mark the islands' British ties. The coat of arms shows the ship Desire, captained by John Davis, who is reputed to have discovered the islands, and the motto 'Desire the Right'.

fm.name: Federated States of Micronesia
fm.symbolism: The light blue represents the Pacific Ocean, and the four white stars stand for the four states: Chuuk, Kosrae, Pohnpei and Yap.

fo.name: Faroe Islands
fo.symbolism: Known as Merkið, 'the banner', it carries a Nordic cross that shows the islands' ties to Scandinavia. White represents the sea foam and bright sky, while red and blue appear in traditional Faroese dress.

fr.name: France
fr.symbolism: Blue and red are the traditional colours of Paris, and white is the 'ancient French colour', which some accounts identify with the monarchy. The three colours are occasionally taken to stand for the revolutionary motto: liberty (blue), equality (white) and fraternity (red).

ga.name: Gabon
ga.symbolism: Green stands for the country's natural resources and extensive forests, yellow for the equator, which cuts across Gabon, and the sun, and blue for the South Atlantic Ocean along its coast.

gb.name: United Kingdom
gb.symbolism: The Union Jack overlays three crosses, each representing a country of the United Kingdom: the red cross of St George for England, the white saltire of St Andrew for Scotland and the red saltire of St Patrick for Northern Ireland. Wales is not represented because it was part of the Kingdom of England when the flag was designed.

gd.name: Grenada
gd.symbolism: Red stands for harmony, unity, courage and vitality, yellow for the sun and the warmth and wisdom of the people, and green for vegetation and agriculture. The nutmeg at the hoist alludes to a main export. The six stars on the border stand for the parishes and the central star for Carriacou and Petite Martinique, counted as the seventh.

ge.name: Georgia
ge.symbolism: The large red cross is St George's cross, and the four smaller Bolnur-Katskhuri crosses are sometimes read as representing the Five Holy Wounds, or alternatively Christ and the four Evangelists.

gf.name: French Guiana
gf.flagNote: Uses the French national flag; the green and yellow flag used locally is unofficial.

gg.name: Guernsey
gg.symbolism: The red St George's cross shows its English connection, and the gold cross inside it recalls William the Conqueror's banner, Guernsey's link to the Duchy of Normandy.

gh.name: Ghana
gh.symbolism: The Pan-African colours stand for the blood of the forefathers who led the struggle for independence (red), the mineral wealth (gold) and the forests and natural wealth (green). The black star symbolises the emancipation of Africa and unity against colonialism.

gi.name: Gibraltar
gi.symbolism: The red castle and golden key come from arms granted by Queen Isabella of Castile. The castle represents the fortress of Gibraltar, and the key its role as the key to Spain, later seen as the key to the Mediterranean.

gl.name: Greenland
gl.symbolism: The white stripe represents the ice cap and the red stripe the ocean. The disc stands for the sun, its red half rising from the sea and its white half for icebergs and pack ice.

gm.name: Gambia
gm.symbolism: Red stands for the sun and the central savanna, blue for the Gambia River, which runs through the country, and green for the forests and agriculture. The thin white stripes stand for peace and unity.

gn.name: Guinea
gn.symbolism: Red stands for the blood of anti-colonial martyrs, the labour of the working classes and the wish for progress, yellow for Guinean gold, the sun and justice, and green for the vegetation and the country's natural wealth. Each corresponds to a part of the national motto: work, justice and solidarity.

gp.name: Guadeloupe
gp.flagNote: Uses the French national flag; the locally used flags are unofficial.

gq.name: Equatorial Guinea
gq.symbolism: Green stands for the country's vegetation, white for peace, red for the blood shed for independence, and the blue triangle for the ocean connecting the mainland to the islands. The arms show a silk-cotton tree and six stars for the mainland and the five islands.

gr.name: Greece
gr.symbolism: The nine stripes have no official meaning, but the popular reading is that they are the nine syllables of the motto 'Freedom or Death'. The blue and white may symbolise the Greek sea and sky, and the white cross in the blue canton symbolises Christianity.

gs.name: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
gs.symbolism: The Blue Ensign and Union Jack mark the territory's British ties. The arms show a lion holding a torch, for the United Kingdom and exploration, with a reindeer, seal and penguin local to the islands, and the motto 'Leo Terram Propriam Protegat', meaning 'let the lion protect its own land'.

gt.name: Guatemala
gt.symbolism: The two sky-blue stripes stand for strength, justice, truth and loyalty, and the white for purity, integrity, firmness and light. The arms hold a quetzal, the national bird and symbol of liberty, a scroll marking the date of independence, crossed rifles for the will to defend the country, a laurel crown for victory and crossed swords for honour.

gu.name: Guam
gu.symbolism: The red border represents the blood spilled during World War II and earlier Spanish sovereignty. The almond-shaped seal recalls a Chamorro sling stone.

gw.name: Guinea-Bissau
gw.symbolism: Red stands for the blood shed in the revolution, yellow for the northern savannas, the sun or mineral wealth, and green for the southern forests and hope. The black star symbolises the leadership of the PAIGC and the people of Africa.

gy.name: Guyana
gy.symbolism: Known as the Golden Arrowhead, it stands for agriculture and forests (green), rivers and water (white), mineral wealth (gold), zeal and dynamism (red) and endurance (black).

hk.name: Hong Kong
hk.symbolism: The white bauhinia flower is the emblem of Hong Kong, and the red field stands for the motherland. The five stars on its petals symbolise Hong Kong people's love for the motherland, and the red and white embody the principle of 'one country, two systems'.

hm.name: Heard Island and McDonald Islands
hm.symbolism: Heard Island and McDonald Islands are an uninhabited Australian territory and use the flag of Australia. Its Union Jack, Commonwealth Star and Southern Cross stand for its British origins, the states and territories, and the southern sky.

hn.name: Honduras
hn.symbolism: Blue stands for the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea and the sky, and white for peace and prosperity. The five blue stars represent the five countries of the former Federal Republic of Central America.

hr.name: Croatia
hr.symbolism: The red, white and blue are pan-Slavic colours, widely associated with romantic nationalism. The chequerboard shield is Croatia's emblem, topped by a crown of five shields for Central Croatia, Dubrovnik, Dalmatia, Istria and Slavonia.

ht.name: Haiti
ht.symbolism: Blue represents the Black Africans and red the mixed-race people, united in the revolution. The arms show a trophy of weapons and a royal palm for independence, topped by the cap of liberty, above the motto 'Unity is strength'.

hu.name: Hungary
hu.symbolism: The colours come from the historic Hungarian coat of arms. The official reading is red for strength, white for fidelity and green for hope.

id.name: Indonesia
id.symbolism: Red stands for courage and white for purity. Another reading takes red as the human body, or physical life, and white as the soul, or spiritual life, together making a complete human being.

ie.name: Ireland
ie.symbolism: Green stands for Roman Catholics and orange for Protestants, the supporters of William of Orange. The white in the centre signifies a lasting truce and hope for union between them.

il.name: Israel
il.symbolism: The white field and blue stripes are based on the Jewish prayer shawl, the tallit, and the blue Star of David is a symbol associated with the Israelite king David.

im.name: Isle of Man
im.symbolism: The triskelion, three armoured legs, is an ancient symbol that has endured as the emblem of the Isle of Man through changes of rule.

in.name: India
in.symbolism: Saffron stands for renunciation and selflessness, white for light and the path of truth, and green for the people's relation to the soil and plant life. The navy blue Ashoka Chakra, with 24 spokes, is the wheel of the law of dharma and stands for motion rather than stagnation.

io.name: British Indian Ocean Territory
io.symbolism: The Union Jack shows the territory's status as a British overseas territory. The blue and white wavy lines depict the waters of the Indian Ocean, where the islands lie, and the palm tree rising above the Tudor Crown is a symbol of the territory.

iq.name: Iraq
iq.symbolism: The red, white and black are the Pan-Arab colours. The green words 'Allahu Akbar' on the white band mean 'God is the greatest'.

ir.name: Iran
ir.symbolism: The green, white and red are historically associated pan-Iranian colours. The red emblem is a stylised form of the word 'Allah', made of four crescents and a sword, and the Takbir 'Allahu Akbar' is repeated 11 times along the edge of each of the green and red bands, 22 times in all, recalling the date of the revolution.

is.name: Iceland
is.symbolism: Red stands for the volcanic fire of the island, white for ice and snow, and blue for the mountains and surrounding sea. The Nordic cross is traditionally associated with Christianity.

it.name: Italy
it.symbolism: The green is a symbol of nature and natural rights. The tricolour became a leading symbol of the movement for Italian unification.

je.name: Jersey
je.symbolism: The red saltire is thought to have signalled the island's neutrality in wars between England and France. The badge of three leopards is Jersey's heraldic device, and the symbol most widely used for the island.

jm.name: Jamaica
jm.symbolism: The gold diagonal cross stands for the wealth of the country and the golden sunshine, the black triangles for the strength and creativity of the people that has overcome difficulties, and the green triangles for the lush vegetation of the island and hope.

jo.name: Jordan
jo.symbolism: The Pan-Arab colours stand for the Abbasid (black), Umayyad (white) and Fatimid (green) caliphates, and the red triangle for the Hashemite dynasty and the Arab Revolt. The seven points of the white star stand for the seven verses of the opening chapter of the Quran.

jp.name: Japan
jp.symbolism: Known as the Hinomaru, 'circle of the sun', the red disc represents the sun, which is central to Japan's name, 'Land of the Rising Sun', and to the legend that the imperial throne descended from the sun goddess Amaterasu.

ke.name: Kenya
ke.symbolism: Black stands for the people of Kenya, red for the blood shed in the fight for independence, green for the land, and white for peace. The traditional African shield and two spears symbolise the country's will to defend itself.

kg.name: Kyrgyzstan
kg.symbolism: Red stands for bravery and the national hero Manas, and the yellow sun for peace and prosperity. Its forty rays represent the forty tribes united by Manas, and the tündük, the crown of a yurt, the home and the universe.

kh.name: Cambodia
kh.symbolism: Red and blue are traditionally the colours of Cambodia, standing for the nation (red, for bravery) and the king (blue, for liberty, cooperation and brotherhood). Angkor Wat stands for integrity, justice and cultural heritage, and for religion.

ki.name: Kiribati
ki.symbolism: The wavy blue and white bands show the Pacific Ocean and the three island groups, the Gilbert, Phoenix and Line Islands. The golden frigatebird stands for power and freedom, and the rising sun for the equatorial location.

km.name: Comoros
km.symbolism: The four stripes and four stars represent the four islands, Grande Comore, Anjouan, Mohéli and Mayotte. The green triangle and white crescent represent Islam, the main religion.

kn.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
kn.symbolism: Green stands for the fertile land, red for the struggle against slavery and colonialism, yellow for sunshine, and the black band for the African heritage. The two white stars represent hope and liberty, and the two islands.

kp.name: North Korea
kp.symbolism: Red stands for revolutionary traditions, white for purity, strength and dignity, and blue for sovereignty, peace and friendship, while the red star represents socialism. State media gives a related reading, with red for the blood shed by Korean patriots.

kr.name: South Korea
kr.symbolism: White stands for peace and purity. The red and blue taegeuk represents the balance of yin and yang, the harmony of opposites, and the four black trigrams stand for heaven, earth, fire and water.

kw.name: Kuwait
kw.symbolism: The Pan-Arab colours each have their own meaning: green stands for the fertile land of Arabia, white for purity and noble deeds, red for the blood on the swords of Muslim warriors, and black for the defeat of enemies in battle.

ky.name: Cayman Islands
ky.symbolism: The Blue Ensign and Union Jack mark the islands' British ties. In the arms, the waves evoke the Caribbean Sea, the three green stars the islands of Grand Cayman, Little Cayman and Cayman Brac, the lion England, the turtle the islands' seafaring and their original name Las Tortugas, and the pineapple the link with Jamaica.

kz.name: Kazakhstan
kz.symbolism: The turquoise blue is of religious significance to the Turkic peoples and so symbolises cultural and ethnic unity, as well as the endless sky and water. The golden sun's 32 rays represent the 32 ethnicities of the Turkic people, and the gold ornament at the hoist, the koshkar-muiz, represents the horns of the ram.

la.name: Laos
la.symbolism: The red stripes stand for the blood shed by the Lao people on both banks of the Mekong in the struggle for freedom and independence, and the blue for the Mekong itself and the nation's prosperity. The white disc symbolises the unity of the Lao people and is also said to be a full moon over the river.

lb.name: Lebanon
lb.symbolism: The green cedar, the 'Land of the Cedars' emblem mentioned often in the Bible, stands for immortality, resilience and hope. The red stripes are commonly read as the blood shed in the struggle for independence, and the white as peace, purity and the snow-capped mountains.

lc.name: Saint Lucia
lc.symbolism: Blue stands for the Atlantic Ocean and Caribbean Sea, gold for sunshine and prosperity, and black and white for the harmonious relationship between the black and white races. The triangles represent the island's twin volcanic Pitons and unity.

li.name: Liechtenstein
li.symbolism: The blue represents the sky and the red the evening fires lit inside houses. The golden crown shows that Liechtenstein is a principality.

lk.name: Sri Lanka
lk.symbolism: The gold lion holding a sword on a maroon field represents the Sinhalese people. The orange stripe represents the Tamils and the green stripe the Moors, Sri Lanka's Muslims, while the yellow border stands for other minorities, and the four bo leaves for the Buddhist values of loving-kindness, compassion, joy and equanimity.

lr.name: Liberia
lr.symbolism: It is modelled on the flag of the United States, reflecting Liberia's founding by free people of colour and former slaves from the United States. The eleven red and white stripes stand for the signers of the Declaration of Independence, and for courage and moral excellence. The white star represents the first independent republic in Africa, above a blue square for the African continent.

ls.name: Lesotho
ls.symbolism: Blue stands for the sky or rain, white for peace and green for prosperity. The black mokorotlo, the Basotho hat, represents Lesotho as a black nation.

lt.name: Lithuania
lt.symbolism: Yellow stands for the sun and prosperity, green for the forests, the countryside, liberty and hope, and red for the blood and bravery of those who died for Lithuania.

lu.name: Luxembourg
lu.symbolism: The red, white and light blue are probably derived from the arms of the County and Duchy of Luxembourg, which combined the lion of the dukes of Limbourg with the striped banner of the early counts.

lv.name: Latvia
lv.symbolism: The dark red symbolises the Latvians' readiness to give their blood for freedom and to defend their sovereignty. According to one legend, a Latgalian leader was wounded in battle and laid on a white sheet, which was stained with his blood except for a narrow central stripe.

ly.name: Libya
ly.symbolism: Red stands for the blood sacrificed for Libya's freedom, black for the dark days under Italian occupation, and green for agriculture, the country's primary wealth, and its future prosperity. The bands also echo the colours of the flags of the regions of Fezzan (red), Cyrenaica (black) and Tripolitania (green). The crescent recalls the Hijra and the beginning of the lunar month in the Islamic calendar, and the star stands for hope and the light of belief in God and country.

ma.name: Morocco
ma.symbolism: Red is the traditional colour of the Alaouite dynasty and stands for the blood of the ancestors and unity. The green pentagram, the seal of Solomon, stands for the five pillars of Islam.

mc.name: Monaco
mc.symbolism: Red and white are the heraldic colours of the House of Grimaldi, the ruling family.

md.name: Moldova
md.symbolism: The blue, yellow and red reflect Moldova's national and cultural affinity with Romania. The arms show an eagle holding an olive branch, symbolising peace, with a shield bearing an aurochs' head, the traditional symbol of Moldavia.

me.name: Montenegro
me.symbolism: The double-headed eagle on the coat of arms is a long-used Montenegrin heraldic symbol, dating back to medieval times.

mf.name: Saint Martin
mf.flagNote: Uses the French national flag; the logo flag used locally is unofficial.

mg.name: Madagascar
mg.symbolism: When the flag was adopted, white was given as purity, red as sovereignty and green as hope. The presidential office now describes red as national unity, green as hope, and white as freedom, security and cleanliness.

mh.name: Marshall Islands
mh.symbolism: Blue stands for the Pacific Ocean. The rising diagonal band represents the equator, and its white and orange parts the Ratak (sunrise) and Ralik (sunset) chains as well as peace and courage. The star above stands for the Northern Hemisphere location, its 24 points for the electoral districts and its four long rays for the cultural centres of Majuro, Jaluit, Wotje and Ebeye.

mk.name: North Macedonia
mk.symbolism: The yellow sun with eight rays reaching the flag's edges derives from the national emblem and represents the 'new sun of liberty' in the anthem 'Denes nad Makedonija', set on a red field.

ml.name: Mali
ml.symbolism: The Pan-African colours stand for the fertility of the land (green), the country's mineral wealth and purity (yellow), and the blood shed for independence (red).

mm.name: Myanmar
mm.symbolism: Yellow represents unity, wisdom and happiness, green fertility, fairness and a peaceful, pleasant, green nation, and red bravery and decisiveness. The white star stands for purity, honesty, compassion and power.

mn.name: Mongolia
mn.symbolism: The blue stripe stands for the eternal blue sky and the red stripes for thriving for eternity, while the yellow symbolises Tibetan Buddhism. The Soyombo at the hoist is a geometric symbol of fire, sun, moon, earth, water and the yin-yang fish that never sleep.

mo.name: Macao
mo.symbolism: The lotus is Macao's floral emblem. The bridge, one of the territory's best-known landmarks, and the water beneath it symbolise Macao's position as a port, and the five stars echo the flag of China, symbolising the relationship with its sovereign state.

mp.name: Northern Mariana Islands
mp.symbolism: The white star represents the United States, the grey latte stone, a pillar used in ancient Chamorro houses, represents the Chamorro people, and the wreath is a mwarmwar, a flower lei, representing the Carolinians. The dark blue background represents the Pacific Ocean and the Mariana Trench.

mq.name: Martinique
mq.symbolism: The red, green and black are the Pan-African colours: red for the blood shed for redemption and liberty, black for the people of African descent, and green for the lush vegetation of the African motherland. It is the preferred symbol of Martinican independence activists.

mr.name: Mauritania
mr.symbolism: The star and crescent, as well as the colour green, are symbols of Islam, and the red stripes represent the blood shed by Mauritanians who fought for independence. The colours are also the Pan-African colours.

ms.name: Montserrat
ms.symbolism: The Blue Ensign and Union Jack mark the island's British ties. The arms show a woman in a green dress, Erin, the personification of Ireland, with a Celtic harp and a cross, honouring the island's Irish settlers.

mt.name: Malta
mt.symbolism: According to tradition, the red and white come from the chequered banner of Count Roger I of Sicily, though historians doubt the story. The George Cross in the corner was awarded by King George VI for the island's bravery during the Second World War.

mu.name: Mauritius
mu.symbolism: Red stands for the struggle for freedom and blue for the Indian Ocean in which Mauritius lies. Yellow stands for the light of freedom shining over the island, and green for its agriculture and its colour throughout the year.

mv.name: Maldives
mv.symbolism: The red stands for the blood of the nation's heroes and their willingness to sacrifice for the country. The green rectangle symbolises peace and prosperity, and the white crescent Islam, the state religion.

mw.name: Malawi
mw.symbolism: Black stands for the indigenous people of Africa, red for the blood of their struggle, and green for nature. The red rising sun represents the dawn of hope and freedom for the continent.

mx.name: Mexico
mx.symbolism: The meaning of the colours has changed over time. The coat of arms recalls the legend of a golden eagle sitting on a nopal cactus and devouring a serpent, the sign that told the Aztecs where to found their city, Tenochtitlan.

my.name: Malaysia
my.symbolism: The 14 stripes represent the equal status of the 13 states and the federal territories, and the star's 14 points their unity. The red, white and blue represent Malaysia's membership of the Commonwealth and its links with the United Kingdom, and the crescent and star represent Islam as the official religion, with yellow standing for the sovereignty of the Malay rulers.

mz.name: Mozambique
mz.symbolism: Red stands for anti-colonial resistance and national defence, green for the soil, golden yellow for the subsoil, black for the African continent, and white for peace and the justice of the struggle. The gun, hoe and book symbolise defence, production and education, and the star the spirit of international solidarity.

na.name: Namibia
na.symbolism: Blue stands for the clear sky, the Atlantic Ocean and the country's water and rain, red for the people and their heroism, green for vegetation, and white for peace and unity. The golden sun stands for life, energy and the country's wealth, and its twelve rays for twelve ethnic groups.

nc.name: New Caledonia
nc.symbolism: This is the French tricolour, the national flag in New Caledonia. Blue and red are the traditional colours of Paris, and white is the 'ancient French colour', which some accounts identify with the monarchy. The three colours are occasionally taken to stand for liberty (blue), equality (white) and fraternity (red).

ne.name: Niger
ne.symbolism: Commonly given readings are that the orange band stands for the Sahara in the north, the white for the Sahel zone, and the green for the fertile south, with the orange disc as the sun; official sources have not confirmed the meanings.

nf.name: Norfolk Island
nf.symbolism: The green Norfolk Island pine, the island's symbol and a native tree, stands in a white band between two green bands. The green symbolises the island's plentiful vegetation and fertile land.

ng.name: Nigeria
ng.symbolism: Green stands for the country's agriculture and natural wealth, and white for peace and unity.

ni.name: Nicaragua
ni.symbolism: The blue bands and the coat of arms reflect Nicaragua's aspiration for the rebirth of the union of the five Central American nations.

nl.name: Netherlands
nl.symbolism: The colours began as the orange, white and blue of William of Orange, leader of the Dutch revolt against Spain, and red gradually replaced orange as a sign of the Republic's growing distance from the House of Orange. By heraldic tradition, red stands for bravery and strength, white for peace and honesty, and blue for vigilance, truth and loyalty.

no.name: Norway
no.symbolism: The Nordic cross represents Christianity. Red, white and blue were chosen as colours of freedom.

np.name: Nepal
np.symbolism: The crimson red stands for the bravery of the Nepalese people and the national flower, the rhododendron, and the blue border for peace and harmony. One popular reading is that the moon and sun stand for peace and hard work, and another that they are symbols of Hinduism and Buddhism, the main religions.

nr.name: Nauru
nr.symbolism: The dark blue stands for the Pacific Ocean, and the thin gold stripe for the equator, with the island just south of it. The white twelve-pointed star represents Nauru itself and its twelve original tribes, and its white also recalls phosphate, a former major natural resource.

nu.name: Niue
nu.symbolism: The Union Jack symbolises the protection granted by the United Kingdom. The yellow field stands for the bright sunshine of Niue and the warm feelings of its people towards New Zealand, the four small stars on the Union Jack depict the Southern Cross for the link with New Zealand, and the blue disc with a larger star represents the deep blue sea around the island.

nz.name: New Zealand
nz.symbolism: The four red stars with white borders show the Southern Cross constellation, signifying New Zealand's place in the South Pacific. The Union Jack reflects its origins as a British colony, and the royal blue is reminiscent of the sea and sky.

om.name: Oman
om.symbolism: White is associated with the Imam, the religious leader, and with peace; green with the fertile Jebel Akhdar, the 'Green Mountains'; and red with the battles fought by the Omani people. The national emblem, a khanjar over crossed swords, shows the traditional weapons of the Omani people.

pa.name: Panama
pa.symbolism: Blue and red stand for the two main political parties, the Conservatives and Liberals, and white for peace between them. The blue star stands for honesty and the red star for authority and law.

pe.name: Peru
pe.symbolism: Red represents the blood spilled by those who fought for independence, and white purity and peace. Legend says General José de San Martín was inspired by the colours of red-and-white flamingos seen on landing in Peru.

pf.name: French Polynesia
pf.symbolism: The outrigger canoe carries a crew of five, shown as stars for the five island groups, on blue waves beneath a golden sun. Red and white are traditional Polynesian colours.

pg.name: Papua New Guinea
pg.symbolism: The Raggiana bird of paradise, a symbol of tribal culture, soars to represent the nation's emergence, and red, black and yellow are colours traditionally used to represent Papua New Guinea. The white stars form the Southern Cross, a common symbol in the Southern Hemisphere, where the constellation can be seen.

ph.name: Philippines
ph.symbolism: The white triangle stands for liberty, equality and fraternity, the golden sun with eight rays for the eight provinces that rose against Spain, and the three stars for the three main island groups: Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao. Blue stands for peace, truth and justice, and red for patriotism and valour.

pk.name: Pakistan
pk.symbolism: Green stands for the Muslim majority, and the white band for religious minorities. The white crescent stands for progress and the star for light and knowledge.

pl.name: Poland
pl.symbolism: The white and red derive from the colours of the coats of arms of the two nations of the old Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, the White Eagle of Poland and the white knight of Lithuania, both on a red shield.

pm.name: Saint Pierre and Miquelon
pm.flagNote: Uses the French national flag; the Grande Hermine flag flown locally is unofficial.

pn.name: Pitcairn Islands
pn.symbolism: The Blue Ensign and Union Jack mark the island's British ties. The arms use blue, yellow and green for the island rising from the Pacific, an anchor and a Bible from HMS Bounty, whose mutineers settled the island, and a wheelbarrow and a sprig of miro tree for the agriculture that helped them survive.

pr.name: Puerto Rico
pr.symbolism: The flag is based on Cuba's with the colours inverted, symbolising the bonds between the Cuban and Puerto Rican independence struggles against Spain. Red stands for the blood shed by warriors, white for liberty, victory and peace, and blue for the sky and coastal waters. The white star stands for the island, and the three sides of the triangle for the three branches of government.

ps.name: Palestine
ps.symbolism: These are the Pan-Arab colours: black for the Abbasid Caliphate, white for the Umayyad Caliphate, green for the Fatimid Caliphate, and the red triangle for the Hashemite dynasty and the Arab Revolt. The flag is a symbol of Palestinian identity.

pt.name: Portugal
pt.symbolism: Green stands for hope and red for the blood of those who died for Portugal. The arms where they meet show a shield of five blue shields, the quinas, with seven castles, set on an armillary sphere recalling the Age of Discovery.

pw.name: Palau
pw.symbolism: Blue stands for the Pacific Ocean, and the golden disc for the full moon, a symbol of peace, love and tranquillity and a traditional time for celebrations and fishing.

py.name: Paraguay
py.symbolism: The red, white and blue are believed to signify independence and liberty. The front shows the national seal, which represents Paraguay's independence, and the back the treasury seal, a lion beneath a Phrygian cap symbolising courage, with the words 'Paz y Justicia' (peace and justice).

qa.name: Qatar
qa.symbolism: The maroon reflects Qatar's heritage in purple dye production, and the white stands for the peace secured by treaties with the British. The nine points of the serrated edge represent Qatar as the ninth 'reconciled emirate' to sign the treaty.

re.name: Réunion
re.flagNote: Uses the French national flag; Réunion has no separate official flag.

ro.name: Romania
ro.symbolism: Blue stands for liberty, yellow for justice, and red for brotherhood, the ideals of the revolution.

rs.name: Serbia
rs.symbolism: The double-headed eagle on the coat of arms recalls the banners of the medieval Serbian kings.

ru.name: Russia
ru.symbolism: The colours are traditionally read as white for nobility and frankness, blue for faithfulness and honesty, and red for courage, generosity and love.

rw.name: Rwanda
rw.symbolism: Blue stands for happiness and peace, yellow for economic development, and green for hope for prosperity. The golden sun represents national unity, transparency and the enlightenment of the Rwandan people.

sa.name: Saudi Arabia
sa.symbolism: The green background represents Islam, and the white Shahada reads: 'There is no god but God, and Muhammad is the Messenger of God.' The sword stands for safety and justice.

sb.name: Solomon Islands
sb.symbolism: The blue evokes the water of the rivers, rain and the Pacific Ocean, and the five white stars stand for the five provinces at independence: Central, Western, Eastern, Malaita and Honiara.

sc.name: Seychelles
sc.symbolism: The bands symbolise a dynamic new country moving into the future. Yellow is for the sun that gives light and life, red for the people's determination to work for the future in unity and love, and white for social justice and harmony.

sd.name: Sudan
sd.symbolism: The Pan-Arab colours stand for Arab unity and independence. Red represents the struggle for independence and the sacrifice of martyrs, white the people, light and optimism, black Sudan itself and the Mahdist revolution, and the green triangle Islam, agriculture and prosperity.

se.name: Sweden
se.symbolism: The blue and gold recall the national arms of three golden crowns on blue. The Nordic cross traditionally represents Christianity, and legend says King Eric IX saw the sun shine against a golden cross in the sky as he landed in Finland.

sg.name: Singapore
sg.symbolism: Red stands for universal brotherhood and equality, and white for pure and lasting virtue. The crescent represents a young, rising nation, and the five stars its ideals: democracy, peace, progress, justice and equality.

sh.name: Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha
sh.flagNote: The territory has no flag of its own; Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha each have their own flag.

si.name: Slovenia
si.symbolism: The white, blue and red are the Carniolan colours, which became the symbol of the Slovene nation. The arms show Mount Triglav, the highest peak, above two wavy blue lines for the Adriatic Sea and rivers, and three golden stars from the arms of the Counts of Celje.

sj.name: Svalbard and Jan Mayen
sj.symbolism: Svalbard and Jan Mayen are Norwegian territories and use the flag of Norway, whose red, white and blue were chosen as colours of freedom.

sk.name: Slovakia
sk.symbolism: The white, blue and red are the Pan-Slavic colours. The coat of arms, with its double cross, is one of the overtly Christian symbols found on national flags, and its three hills are enlarged to emphasise it as a national symbol.

sl.name: Sierra Leone
sl.symbolism: Green stands for agriculture, natural resources and the mountains, white for unity and justice, and blue for the Atlantic Ocean and the natural harbour of Freetown, the capital.

sm.name: San Marino
sm.symbolism: The white stands for peace and the light blue for liberty. The arms show three towers on three peaks of Mount Titano, and the motto 'Libertas', meaning freedom.

sn.name: Senegal
sn.symbolism: The Pan-African colours: green is the colour of the Prophet in Islam and of hope and fertility to others, yellow stands for wealth and the progress of the economy, and red for life and the nation's sacrifice and determination to fight underdevelopment. The green star is linked to the Serer star Yooniir.

so.name: Somalia
so.symbolism: The light blue was chosen in tribute to the United Nations, which helped form Somalia as a trust territory, and also denotes the sky and the seas that flank the country. The five points of the white star represent the five regions where Somalis live.

sr.name: Suriname
sr.symbolism: Green stands for the fertility and agricultural richness of the land, white for freedom and justice, and red for progress and hope. The yellow star stands for unity, the sacrifices made for independence and a golden future.

ss.name: South Sudan
ss.symbolism: Black stands for the people, red for the blood shed for freedom, green for the land, white for peace, and the blue triangle for the Nile. The yellow star stands for unity of the states.

st.name: São Tomé and Príncipe
st.symbolism: The green, yellow and red are the Pan-African colours and represent the independence movement: green for the lush vegetation, yellow for the sun or cocoa, and the red triangle for equality. The two black stars stand for the islands of São Tomé and Príncipe.

sv.name: El Salvador
sv.symbolism: The top and bottom blue stripes symbolise the Pacific and Atlantic Oceans, the latter intended to represent Central America as a whole, and the white stripe symbolises peace. The coat of arms carries the motto 'God, Union, Liberty'.

sx.name: Sint Maarten
sx.symbolism: The red, white and blue evoke the flag of the Netherlands, Sint Maarten's mother country; blue represents the sea and sky and red the blood of Sint Maarteners. On the coat of arms, green stands for the fertility of the land and yellow for the energy of the islanders, while the orange and light blue allude to the colours of the Dutch monarchy.

sy.name: Syria
sy.symbolism: Green stands for the Rashidun Caliphate, white for the Umayyad Caliphate and black for the Abbasid Caliphate. The three red stars originally represented the states of Aleppo, Damascus and Deir ez-Zor.

sz.name: Eswatini
sz.symbolism: The red stands for past battles, the blue for peace and stability, and the yellow for the country's resources. The central Nguni shield and two spears symbolise protection from the country's enemies.

tc.name: Turks and Caicos Islands
tc.symbolism: The Blue Ensign and Union Jack mark the islands' British ties. On the shield, the cactus, which resembles the traditional Turkish fez, gives the islands the first half of their name.

td.name: Chad
td.symbolism: The indigo blue represents Lake Chad and the Black African heritage, the yellow the sands of the Sahara desert, and the red the bloodshed for independence.

tf.name: French Southern and Antarctic Lands
tf.symbolism: The blue field stands for the Southern Ocean, and the French tricolour in the corner marks the territory's link to France. The white monogram TAAF, shaped like an anchor, is surrounded by five stars, sometimes thought to represent the territory's five districts.

tg.name: Togo
tg.symbolism: Green stands for forests, agriculture and hope, yellow for natural resources, faith and maturity, and red for the blood shed by those who fought for independence. The white star stands for peace, intelligence and light, and the five stripes for the five regions of Togo.

th.name: Thailand
th.symbolism: The colours are said to stand for nation, religion and king: red for the land and people, white for religion and blue for the monarchy, blue being the auspicious colour of King Rama VI.

tj.name: Tajikistan
tj.symbolism: Red stands for the unity of the nation, victory and the sunrise, white for purity and cotton, and green for the generosity of nature and fertile valleys. The crown represents the Samanid dynasty and the Tajik people, and the seven stars the number seven's meaning of perfection and happiness in Persian mythology.

tk.name: Tokelau
tk.symbolism: The yellow canoe symbolises Tokelau's journey towards finding the best governance structure for its people, and the Southern Cross is a navigational aid for that journey, on a blue field for the ocean.

tl.name: Timor-Leste
tl.symbolism: Red stands for the struggle for national liberation, black for the obscurantism that must be overcome, and yellow for the wealth of the country. The white star is the light that guides and represents peace.

tm.name: Turkmenistan
tm.symbolism: The five carpet guls on the red band at the hoist stand for the five major tribes of Turkmenistan, and the olive branches for the country's permanent neutrality. No official explanation is given for the colours, but the five stars are said to represent the five regions, and the crescent and stars together a bright future.

tn.name: Tunisia
tn.symbolism: Red stands for the blood of martyrs, and the white disc for peace and the sun. The crescent and five-pointed star are symbols of Islam.

to.name: Tonga
to.symbolism: Red stands for the blood of Christ, and the red cross for Christianity, as Tonga is a deeply Christian country. The white canton stands for purity.

tr.name: Türkiye
tr.symbolism: The origin of the red field and the white crescent and star is unclear, and several myths are attached to them. The crescent may derive from the symbol of ancient Byzantium, and a popular legend says the crescent and star were the moon and a star reflected in blood after a battle.

tt.name: Trinidad and Tobago
tt.symbolism: Red, black and white stand for fire (the sun and courage), earth (dedication) and water (purity and equality).

tv.name: Tuvalu
tv.symbolism: Light blue stands for the Pacific Ocean, and the Union Jack for ties to the United Kingdom and the Commonwealth. The nine yellow stars represent the nine islands; the name Tuvalu means 'eight standing together', after the original eight inhabited islands.

tw.name: Taiwan
tw.symbolism: Red stands for the blood of the revolutionaries and for the people's livelihood and fraternity, blue for nationalism and liberty, and the white sun for democracy and equality. Its 12 rays stand for the 12 months and the 12 traditional Chinese hours of the day.

tz.name: Tanzania
tz.symbolism: Green stands for the natural vegetation and rich agricultural resources, black for the Swahili people, and the thin yellow stripes for the country's mineral wealth. Blue stands for the Indian Ocean and lakes, and the colours combine those of Tanganyika and Zanzibar, the two states that formed Tanzania.

ua.name: Ukraine
ua.symbolism: Yellow and blue are rooted in traditional ceremonies from pre-Christian times, where they reflected fire and water. The colours were also common on the coats of arms of Galicia, and the arms of Lviv remain a golden lion on a blue field.

ug.name: Uganda
ug.symbolism: Black symbolises the Ugandan people, yellow sunshine and red brotherhood. The crested crane is the national bird, a symbol of good fortune, longevity and wealth among the Baganda.

um.name: United States Minor Outlying Islands
um.symbolism: The United States Minor Outlying Islands use the flag of the United States, whose stripes represent the original thirteen colonies and whose stars represent the states.

us.name: United States
us.symbolism: The thirteen stripes represent the original thirteen colonies and the 50 stars the 50 states. Red stands for valour and hardiness, white for purity and innocence, and blue for vigilance, perseverance and justice.

uy.name: Uruguay
uy.symbolism: The nine stripes stand for the nine original departments of Uruguay, and the golden Sun of May represents the May Revolution.

uz.name: Uzbekistan
uz.symbolism: There is no official meaning for the elements, but common readings are blue for the sky and clear water, white for peace and good luck, green for nature and harvest, and the thin red lines for the power of life. The crescent is a symbol of a new nation and the twelve stars recall the provinces and the traditional calendar.

va.name: Vatican City
va.symbolism: The flag is a symbol of Catholic faith and identity, since the papacy that governs Vatican City leads the worldwide Catholic Church. Its emblem, a papal tiara above the crossed keys of Saint Peter, stands for papal authority.

vc.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
vc.symbolism: Blue stands for the sky and sea, gold for the sand, the sunshine and the bright spirit of the islanders, and green for the lush vegetation and vitality. The three diamonds evoke the islands' nicknames, the 'Gems of the Antilles' and the 'Jewels of the Caribbean'.

ve.name: Venezuela
ve.symbolism: Traditionally, yellow stands for the wealth of the land, red for courage, and blue for independence from Spain, 'golden' America separated from bloody Spain by the sea. The eight stars stand for the seven provinces that signed the declaration of independence and Guayana.

vg.name: British Virgin Islands
vg.symbolism: The Blue Ensign and Union Jack mark the islands' British ties. The shield shows Saint Ursula holding a flaming gold oil lamp, surrounded by eleven more lamps for her 11,000 virgin followers.

vi.name: United States Virgin Islands
vi.symbolism: The yellow eagle holds a sprig of laurel for victory in one talon and three blue arrows in the other, for the three major islands: Saint Croix, Saint Thomas and Saint John. The letters V and I stand for Virgin Islands.

vn.name: Vietnam
vn.symbolism: Red stands for the revolution and the blood shed for independence. The yellow star's five points stand for the main classes of society: workers, peasants, intellectuals, traders and soldiers.

vu.name: Vanuatu
vu.symbolism: Green stands for the richness of the islands, red for blood, which unites humanity, and black for the Melanesian ni-Vanuatu people. The yellow Y represents the shape of the islands on the map and the light of the Gospel, and the boar's tusk, a symbol of custom, tradition and prosperity, is shown with two namele leaves for peace; their 39 leaflets stand for the original 39 members of parliament.

wf.name: Wallis and Futuna
wf.flagNote: Uses the French national flag; the red saltire flag used locally is unofficial.

ws.name: Samoa
ws.symbolism: The flag law gives no official meaning to the design, but red is reported to stand for courage, white for purity and blue for freedom. The five white stars form the Southern Cross, a common motif on flags of the Southern Hemisphere.

ye.name: Yemen
ye.symbolism: The Pan-Arab colours: red stands for the blood of martyrs and the unity of the nation, white for a bright future, and black for the dark past.

yt.name: Mayotte
yt.flagNote: Uses the French national flag; Mayotte has no official flag of its own.

za.name: South Africa
za.symbolism: The Y or V shape stands for the convergence of diverse elements within South African society, taking the road ahead in unity. The colours have no official symbolism, though the gold is said to signify the country's mineral wealth.

zm.name: Zambia
zm.symbolism: Green stands for the country's natural resources and vegetation, red for the struggle for freedom, black for the people, and orange for the mineral wealth, especially copper. The orange eagle stands for the people's ability to rise above problems.

zw.name: Zimbabwe
zw.symbolism: Green stands for agriculture, yellow for mineral wealth, red for the blood shed in the struggle for freedom, and black for the African majority. The white triangle stands for peace, the red star for the nation's hope, and the soapstone bird for the heritage of Great Zimbabwe.
